def-periodic-fourier-collocation-grid:
## Definition

Let $N\ge2$ be an integer, let $x_j=2\pi j/N$ for $j=0,\ldots,N-1$, and identify $x_N$ with $x_0$ periodically. The real trigonometric interpolation space is
$$
\mathcal T_N=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{1,\cos(kx),\sin(kx):1\le k\le (N-1)/2\},&N\text{ odd},\\
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{1,\cos(kx),\sin(kx):1\le k<N/2\}\oplus\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\cos(Nx/2)\},&N\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$
For real nodal data $U=(U_0,\ldots,U_{N-1})$, define its periodic Fourier interpolant by
$$
I_NU(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}U_jL_j(x),
$$
where, for $N=2K+1$,
$$
L_j(x)=\frac1N\left(1+2\sum_{k=1}^{K}\cos(k(x-x_j))\right),
$$
and, for $N=2K$,
$$
L_j(x)=\frac1N\left(1+2\sum_{k=1}^{K-1}\cos(k(x-x_j))+\cos(K(x-x_j))\right).
$$
Thus the even-grid Nyquist component is the real cosine $\cos(Nx/2)$ only. Its sampled derivative is defined by differentiating this interpolant; the resulting Nyquist derivative values are zero at every grid point.
lem-periodic-fourier-mode-aliasing-under:
## Statement

Let $N\ge2$ and $x_j=2\pi j/N$. If integers $k,r$ satisfy $k\equiv r\pmod N$, then
$$
e^{ikx_j}=e^{irx_j}\qquad(0\le j<N).
$$
Consequently, sampling a product of Fourier modes with frequencies $k_1,\ldots,k_s$ gives the same nodal data as the single mode whose frequency is the sum $\sum_{\ell=1}^s k_\ell$ reduced modulo $N$. The interpolant is the unique member of the frequency space in [[def-periodic-fourier-collocation-grid]] with those data.
alg-periodic-fourier-collocation-differe:
## Definition

Input an integer $N\ge2$ and real data $U_0,\ldots,U_{N-1}$ on the grid of [[def-periodic-fourier-collocation-grid]]. Set $K=(N-1)/2$ when $N$ is odd and $K=N/2$ when $N$ is even. Form the $(N\times N)$ matrix
$$
(D_N)_{ij}=
\begin{cases}
-\dfrac2N\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{K}k\sin(k(x_i-x_j)),&N\text{ odd},\\[1.2ex]
-\dfrac2N\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{K-1}k\sin(k(x_i-x_j)),&N\text{ even},
\end{cases}
\qquad 0\le i,j<N.
$$
The algorithm returns $D_N$ and the derivative vector $D_NU$. In the even case it omits the derivative of the Nyquist cosine because $\sin((N/2)(x_i-x_j))=0$ for grid indices $i,j$. All operations are in exact real arithmetic; no floating-point stability or error guarantee is asserted.
thm-periodic-fourier-collocation-differe:
## Statement

Let $N\ge2$, let $U=(U_j)_{j=0}^{N-1}\in\mathbb R^N$, and let $p=I_NU\in\mathcal T_N$ be the interpolant defined in [[def-periodic-fourier-collocation-grid]]. The matrix [[alg-periodic-fourier-collocation-differentiation-matrix]] satisfies
$$
(D_NU)_i=p'(x_i),\qquad 0\le i<N.
$$
For even $N$, this statement includes the Nyquist cosine mode, whose derivative vanishes at the grid nodes.
def-chebyshev-gauss-lobatto-collocation-:
## Definition

Let $N\ge1$ be an integer and put $x_j=\cos(j\pi/N)$ for $j=0,\ldots,N$. The ordering is decreasing: $x_0=1$ and $x_N=-1$. These are the Chebyshev–Gauss–Lobatto nodes; [[thm-chebyshev-multiple-angle-identities]] gives $T_N(x_j)=(-1)^j$. They are distinct because cosine is strictly decreasing on $[0,\pi]$ by [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]].

For interpolation using [[def-cardinal-polynomial-interpolation]], use the increasing reindexing $z_k=x_{N-k}$, $k=0,\ldots,N$. For descending-grid data $U_j$, the corresponding increasing data are $Y_k=U_{N-k}$.

For nodal data $U_0,\ldots,U_N$, define $I_N^LU$ to be the cardinal interpolant of $(Y_k)_{k=0}^N$ at $(z_k)_{k=0}^N$. For a function $f$ defined on the interval, write $I_N^Lf$ for the interpolant of its nodal values. The increasing-node interpolation theorem [[thm-cardinal-polynomial-interpolant-exists-uniquely]] makes this polynomial unique.
lem-chebyshev-lobatto-mode-aliasing:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$, let $x_j=\cos(j\pi/N)$, and let $I_N^L$ denote degree-at-most-$N$ interpolation on these nodes. For every integer $n\ge0$, let $\rho_N(n)$ be the unique integer $r\in\{0,\ldots,N\}$ congruent to either $n$ or $-n$ modulo $2N$. Then
$$
I_N^L T_n=T_{\rho_N(n)}.
$$
In particular, sampling a Chebyshev series on the Lobatto grid can fold every degree $n>N$ to a degree at most $N$.
alg-chebyshev-gauss-lobatto-differentiat:
## Definition

Input $N\ge1$ and real nodal values $U_0,\ldots,U_N$ at the descending grid $x_j=\cos(j\pi/N)$ from [[def-chebyshev-gauss-lobatto-collocation-grid]]. Set $z_k=x_{N-k}$ and $Y_k=U_{N-k}$, so $z_0<\cdots<z_N$. Form the cardinal polynomials $\ell_k$ for the increasing nodes $z_0,\ldots,z_N$ by [[def-cardinal-polynomial-interpolation]]. Define
$$
(D_N)_{ij}=\ell_{N-j}'(x_i),\qquad 0\le i,j\le N,
$$
and return the derivative vector $D_NU$. Equivalently, form $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^NY_k\ell_k(x)$ and return $(p'(x_i))_{i=0}^N$. The procedure is exact-real arithmetic and makes no stability claim for a floating-point implementation.
thm-chebyshev-gauss-lobatto-differentiat:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$, let $U_j\in\mathbb R$ be data on the nodes $x_j=\cos(j\pi/N)$, and let $p$ be the unique polynomial of degree at most $N$ with $p(x_j)=U_j$. The matrix [[alg-chebyshev-gauss-lobatto-differentiation-matrix]] satisfies
$$
(D_NU)_i=p'(x_i),\qquad 0\le i\le N.
$$
In particular, applying $D_N$ twice gives $p''(x_i)$ at each node.
alg-chebyshev-dirichlet-bvp-collocation-:
## Definition

Input an integer $N\ge2$, real functions $a,b,f$ given at the Chebyshev–Gauss–Lobatto nodes $x_j=\cos(j\pi/N)$, and endpoint data $g_-,g_+\in\mathbb R$. The continuous BVP being discretized is
$$
-u''(x)+a(x)u'(x)+b(x)u(x)=f(x),\quad -1<x<1,\qquad u(-1)=g_-,\quad u(1)=g_+.
$$
The finite algorithm uses only the values at the nodes and does not assume a continuous BVP solvability theorem. Construct the Chebyshev differentiation matrix $D_N$ by [[alg-chebyshev-gauss-lobatto-differentiation-matrix]] and set $D_N^{(2)}=D_ND_N$. For each interior row $i=1,\ldots,N-1$ and each column $j=0,\ldots,N$, put
$$
C_{ij}=-(D_N^{(2)})_{ij}+a(x_i)(D_N)_{ij}+b(x_i)\delta_{ij}.
$$
Let $A=(C_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le N-1}$ and $r_i=f(x_i)-C_{i0}g_+-C_{iN}g_-$. If $A$ is singular, return status singular-interior-matrix and the matrix $A$. If $A$ is invertible, solve $AU_I=r$, set $U_0=g_+$ and $U_N=g_-$, and return success with $U=(U_0,U_1,\ldots,U_N)$. This exact-arithmetic finite solve asserts no unconditional nonsingularity, stability, convergence, or PDE error bound.
thm-chebyshev-dirichlet-collocation-stat:
## Statement

For the algorithm [[alg-chebyshev-dirichlet-bvp-collocation-boundary-elimination]], a success output is the unique nodal vector with $U_0=g_+$, $U_N=g_-$ satisfying
$$
-(D_N^{(2)}U)_i+a(x_i)(D_NU)_i+b(x_i)U_i=f(x_i),\qquad 1\le i<N,
$$
where $D_N$ is the exact Chebyshev–Gauss–Lobatto differentiation matrix and $D_N^{(2)}=D_ND_N$. If the interior matrix is singular, the algorithm returns singular-interior-matrix and makes no claim about existence or uniqueness for the given right-hand side.
def-chebyshev-arcsine-weighted-l2-pairin:
## Definition

For continuous real functions $f,g$ on $[-1,1]$, define
$$
\langle f,g\rangle_C:=\int_0^\pi f(\cos\theta)g(\cos\theta)\,d\theta,\qquad \|f\|_C^2:=\langle f,f\rangle_C.
$$
This is the arcsine-weighted pairing on the compact Chebyshev interval: in the variable $x=\cos\theta$ its weight is $\omega_C(x)=(1-x^2)^{-1/2}$ for $-1<x<1$. The angular integral is the endpoint convention, so no endpoint value of the singular density is required.
lem-chebyshev-polynomials-orthogonal-in-:
## Statement

Under the pairing of [[def-chebyshev-arcsine-weighted-l2-pairing]],
$$
\langle T_m,T_n\rangle_C=
\begin{cases}
\pi,&m=n=0,\\
\pi/2,&m=n\ge1,\\
0,&m\ne n.
\end{cases}
$$
The polynomials $T_0,T_1,\ldots$ form a basis of the real polynomial space, and the pairing is positive definite on continuous real functions on $[-1,1]$. If a continuous real function $h$ satisfies $\langle h,T_n\rangle_C=0$ for every $n\ge0$, then $h=0$ on $[-1,1]$.
def-chebyshev-weighted-spectral-sobolev-:
## Definition

For $s\ge0$, define $H_C^s$ to be the completion of finite Chebyshev sums $p=\sum_{n=0}^{M}c_nT_n$ in the norm
$$
\|p\|_{H_C^s}^2=\pi|c_0|^2+\frac{\pi}{2}\sum_{n=1}^{M}(1+n^2)^s|c_n|^2.
$$
By [[lem-chebyshev-polynomials-orthogonal-in-arcsine-weight]], the coefficients of a finite sum are unique and this is a norm. The underlying $L_C^2$ norm is the arcsine-weighted norm from [[def-chebyshev-arcsine-weighted-l2-pairing]]. This is the spectral Sobolev scale for the named weight and domain; it is defined by Chebyshev coefficients, and no equivalence with an unweighted derivative-based Sobolev norm is asserted.

For $u=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nT_n$ in this completion, define the degree-$N$ orthogonal projection by
$$
\Pi_Nu=\sum_{n=0}^{N}c_nT_n.
$$
The coefficient series and the projection are well-defined by the orthogonality and positive coefficient norm above.
thm-chebyshev-weighted-orthogonal-projec:
## Statement

Let $s\ge0$, $N\ge0$, and $u\in H_C^s$ as defined in [[def-chebyshev-weighted-spectral-sobolev-scale]]. Then
$$
\|u-\Pi_Nu\|_C\le (1+(N+1)^2)^{-s/2}\|u\|_{H_C^s}.
$$
Thus the weighted projection error is $O(N^{-s})$ when the data belong to this explicitly defined weighted spectral Sobolev space.
thm-chebyshev-lobatto-interpolation-near:
## Statement

For $f\in C[-1,1]$ and $N\ge0$, let $E_N(f)$ and $\Lambda_N^L$ be the best uniform error and the Lebesgue constant from [[def-best-uniform-polynomial-approximation-error-and-chebyshev-interpolants]]. Then
$$
\|f-I_N^Lf\|_C\le \sqrt{\pi}\,(1+\Lambda_N^L)E_N(f),
$$
where $\|\cdot\|_C$ is the arcsine-weighted norm of [[def-chebyshev-arcsine-weighted-l2-pairing]].
thm-chebyshev-lobatto-interpolation-rate:
## Statement

Let $s>1/2$, $N\ge1$, and $u=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nT_n\in H_C^s$. Then the series converges uniformly, its nodal interpolant $I_N^Lu$ is defined, and
$$
\|u-I_N^Lu\|_C\le C_sN^{-s}\|u\|_{H_C^s},\qquad
C_s=1+2\sqrt{1+\frac1{2s-1}}.
$$
thm-chebyshev-lobatto-pointwise-remainde:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$ and $f\in C^{N+1}([-1,1])$. Let $I_N^Lf$ be interpolation at the nodes $x_j=\cos(j\pi/N)$. Then
$$
\|f-I_N^Lf\|_C
\le \sqrt{\pi}\,\frac{2^{1-N}}{(N+1)!}\max_{x\in[-1,1]}|f^{(N+1)}(x)|.
$$
thm-chebyshev-lobatto-interpolation-expo:
## Statement

Let $\rho>1$, and let $E_\rho$ be the closed Bernstein ellipse
$$
E_\rho=\left\{\frac{\rho e^{it}+\rho^{-1}e^{-it}}2:0\le t\le2\pi\right\}
$$
together with its interior. Suppose $f$ is real-valued on $[-1,1]$, extends holomorphically to an open neighborhood of $E_\rho$, and satisfies $|f(z)|\le M$ on $E_\rho$. Then for every $N\ge1$,
$$
\|f-I_N^Lf\|_C\le \frac{4\sqrt{\pi}M}{\rho-1}\rho^{-N}.
$$
alg-chebyshev-composite-simpson-weighted:
## Definition

Input a polynomial degree $N\ge0$ and an even integer $M\ge2$ specifying the number of uniform subintervals of $[0,\pi]$. For $0\le i,j\le N$, form
$$
g_{ij}(\theta)=T_i(\cos\theta)T_j(\cos\theta)
$$
and return
$$
M^{S}_{ij}:=Q_S(g_{ij};0,\pi,M),
$$
where $Q_S$ is the composite Simpson procedure from [[alg-composite-simpson-rule]]. By the Chebyshev multiple-angle identity, $g_{ij}(\theta)=\cos(i\theta)\cos(j\theta)$, so this is the composite-Simpson approximation of the corresponding arcsine-weighted mass entry. The procedure uses exact real arithmetic and asserts no quadrature or floating-point accuracy beyond a separately proved bound.
thm-composite-simpson-error-for-chebyshe:
## Statement

Let $N\ge0$, let $M\ge2$ be even, put $h=\pi/M$, and let $G_{ij}=\langle T_i,T_j\rangle_C$ be the exact weighted mass entry from [[def-chebyshev-arcsine-weighted-l2-pairing]]. The approximation $M^S_{ij}$ from [[alg-chebyshev-composite-simpson-weighted-mass-matrix]] satisfies
$$
|G_{ij}-M^S_{ij}|\le \frac{\pi h^4}{180}(i+j)^4,\qquad 0\le i,j\le N.
$$
def-weighted-orthogonal-polynomial-galer:
## Definition

Let $\mu$ be a finite positive Borel measure on a compact interval $[a,b]$ with infinite relative support. For each integer $N\ge0$, the moment data $(a,b,m=N+1,r=2N+1,\mu)$ satisfy the hypotheses of [[def-gauss-moment-data]]. Let $p_0,\ldots,p_N$ be the monic orthogonal polynomials supplied by [[thm-monic-gauss-orthogonal-polynomials-exist-uniquely]], and write
$$
h_n=\int_{[a,b]}p_n(x)^2\,d\mu(x)>0.
$$
The finite-dimensional weighted Galerkin space is
$$
V_N(\mu)=\operatorname{span}\{p_0,\ldots,p_N\}\subset L^2(\mu).
$$
Here $L^2(\mu)$ means measurable functions with finite integral of the squared absolute value, modulo equality $\mu$-almost everywhere.

For a coefficient sequence $(c_n)_{n\ge0}$ with $\sum_{n\ge0}(1+n^2)^s|c_n|^2h_n<\infty$, define its weighted spectral Sobolev norm by
$$
\left\|\sum_{n\ge0}c_np_n\right\|_{H^s_\mu}^2
=\sum_{n\ge0}(1+n^2)^s|c_n|^2h_n,\qquad s\ge0.
$$
The associated orthogonal Galerkin projection is $\Pi_N(\sum_{n\ge0}c_np_n)=\sum_{n=0}^Nc_np_n$. This coefficient-defined scale is specific to the weight $\mu$ and the selected orthogonal-polynomial family; no equivalence with a derivative-based Sobolev norm is asserted here.
thm-weighted-orthogonal-polynomial-galer:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[def-weighted-orthogonal-polynomial-galerkin-space]], for every real measurable $u$ such that $\int|u p_j|\,d\mu<\infty$ for $0\le j\le N$, the formula
$$
\Pi_Nu=\sum_{j=0}^{N}\frac{\int u(x)p_j(x)\,d\mu(x)}{h_j}\,p_j
$$
is finite and defines the unique element of $V_N(\mu)$ whose residual is orthogonal to every $p_i$, $0\le i\le N$.
alg-gaussian-orthogonal-polynomial-galer:
## Definition

Input a degree $N\ge0$, the monic orthogonal basis $p_0,\ldots,p_N$ and the $(N+1)$-node Gaussian rule for the same positive measure $\mu$ from [[def-gauss-quadrature-rule]]. With Gaussian nodes $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_{N+1}$ and weights $w_1,\ldots,w_{N+1}$, output the matrix
$$
M_{ij}^{G}:=\sum_{r=1}^{N+1}w_r p_i(\xi_r)p_j(\xi_r),\qquad 0\le i,j\le N.
$$
The inputs are admissible only when the moment data have order at least $2N+1$ and the rule nodes, weights, and basis all use the same measure. The algorithm performs the displayed finite exact-arithmetic sums; no floating-point conditioning claim is made.
thm-gaussian-orthogonal-polynomial-galer:
## Statement

Let $N\ge0$, take moment data of order $2N+1$ for a finite positive measure $\mu$ with support containing at least $N+2$ points, and use its $(N+1)$-node Gaussian rule and orthogonal polynomials $p_0,\ldots,p_N$. The matrix from [[alg-gaussian-orthogonal-polynomial-galerkin-mass-matrix]] has entries
$$
M_{ij}^{G}=\int p_i(x)p_j(x)\,d\mu(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&i\ne j,\\
h_i,&i=j.
\end{cases}
$$
def-legendre-polynomial-family-and-l2-pa:
## Definition

For each integer $n\ge0$, define the Legendre polynomial
$$
P_n(x):=\frac{1}{2^n n!}\frac{d^n}{dx^n}(x^2-1)^n,
$$
with $n!$ as in [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]] and repeated derivatives as in [[def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness]]. Define the unweighted pairing of real polynomials by
$$
\langle p,q\rangle_L:=\int_{-1}^1p(x)q(x)\,dx,\qquad \|p\|_L^2:=\langle p,p\rangle_L.
$$
The integral is the ordinary integral of a continuous function. The normalization and all polynomial identities needed for the orthogonal Galerkin scale are proved in [[lem-legendre-weighted-derivative-orthogonality-and-norm]].
lem-legendre-weighted-derivative-orthogo:
## Statement

For $m,n\ge0$, the polynomials of [[def-legendre-polynomial-family-and-l2-pairing]] satisfy
$$
\int_{-1}^1P_n(x)P_m(x)\,dx=\frac{2}{2n+1}\,\delta_{mn},
\qquad
\int_{-1}^1(1-x^2)P_n'(x)P_m'(x)\,dx=\frac{2n(n+1)}{2n+1}\,\delta_{mn},
$$
where $\delta_{mn}=1$ if $m=n$ and $0$ otherwise. Each $P_n$ has degree $n$ and nonzero leading coefficient, so $P_0,\ldots,P_N$ form a basis of polynomials of degree at most $N$.
def-legendre-weighted-sobolev-scale:
## Definition

For $s\ge0$, define $H_L^s$ as the completion of finite Legendre sums $p=\sum_{n=0}^Mc_nP_n$ in the coefficient norm
$$
\|p\|_{H_L^s}^2=\sum_{n=0}^M(1+n(n+1))^s\frac{2}{2n+1}|c_n|^2.
$$
The coefficients are unique because the polynomials have distinct degrees by [[lem-legendre-weighted-derivative-orthogonality-and-norm]]. At $s=0$ this norm is exactly the unweighted $L^2([-1,1])$ norm on finite sums, by the same lemma; its completion is denoted $L_L^2$. Define the degree-$N$ orthogonal projection on finite sums by
$$
\Pi_Nu=\sum_{n=0}^Nc_nP_n.
$$
It extends to the coefficient completion by truncation. This explicitly coefficient-defined scale uses the Legendre weight $1$ on $[-1,1]$; no equivalence with an unweighted derivative-based Sobolev norm is asserted here.
thm-legendre-weighted-projection-error-r:
## Statement

Let $s\ge0$, $N\ge0$, and $u=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nP_n\in H_L^s$ from [[def-legendre-weighted-sobolev-scale]]. Then
$$
\|u-\Pi_Nu\|_{L_L^2}\le(1+(N+1)(N+2))^{-s/2}\|u\|_{H_L^s}.
$$
